base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning assistant. Help the user plan their family Christmas dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and any logistics. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active guest's current dietary constraints and any special arrangements like packed plates for absent guests.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm starting to plan our family Christmas dinner and could use some help organizing everything. We're hosting at our place this year.

flow_info.value: Coming to dinner: me and my husband, my sister Rachel, my brother-in-law Tom, and my mom
Tom was diagnosed with celiac disease last spring
Mom has had type 2 diabetes for years, she's pretty careful about it
So that's five of us. Think a 12-pound turkey is enough or should I go bigger?
My Uncle Frank just called — he's driving down from Vermont after all, so that's six now. He had a knee replacement surgery three weeks ago so he's still on blood thinners
Rachel just texted me — she's been having really bad morning sickness all day and doesn't think she can make it to dinner. She asked if I could save her a plate though, she'll pick it up tomorrow
Tom is still coming even though Rachel isn't — he said he'll bring the kids over and pick up Rachel's plate on the way home
Oh great news — Mom told me her doctor took her off the diabetes medication last month, her A1C has been normal for a full year now. Doctor said she doesn't need to restrict sugar anymore
What time should I plan to have everything ready? Uncle Frank said he can't get here before 4pm because of the drive
Here's what I'm thinking for the menu: honey-glazed ham, beef Wellington with puff pastry, smoked salmon crostini, cranberry walnut salad, and eggnog cheesecake. How does that look?

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw or undercooked fish, unpasteurized cheese, or high-mercury fish
inference_chain: Seven months pregnant → pregnancy dietary restrictions
Pregnancy → avoid raw/undercooked fish, unpasteurized dairy, high-mercury fish

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or products containing them
constraints.surface_form: Tom was diagnosed with celiac disease last spring
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
No gluten → no regular bread, pastry, most crusts, many sauces

constraints.value: Should avoid foods very high in vitamin K (like large amounts of leafy greens) and avoid alcohol, as these interact with blood thinners
constraints.surface_form: Uncle Frank had knee replacement surgery three weeks ago and is still on blood thinners
inference_chain: Knee replacement three weeks ago → post-surgical recovery
Blood thinners → avoid excessive vitamin K (counteracts medication) and alcohol (increases bleeding risk)

hidden_state.value: You are planning a family Christmas dinner at your house. You will introduce 5 guests with various health conditions, then Uncle Frank joins late with his own constraint. Rachel drops out but wants a saved plate. Mom's diabetes restriction gets lifted. At the end you will share a specific menu and ask how it looks — you must NOT hint at any specific dietary problems yourself, just ask for the assistant's opinion on the menu.

You are a calm, warm family organizer. You always refer to family members by name in third person (e.g. 'Rachel texted me...', 'Mom told me...'). You never express frustration or impatience even when plans keep changing — it's just how family holidays go. You treat each update as normal holiday coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for family updates

ground_truth.answer: Beef Wellington with puff pastry is problematic: puff pastry contains wheat flour (gluten), which Tom cannot eat due to celiac disease. Smoked salmon crostini has two issues: the crostini bread base contains gluten (Tom, celiac), and smoked salmon should not be included on Rachel's saved plate since she is seven months pregnant and should avoid smoked/raw fish. Eggnog cheesecake is problematic for Uncle Frank: traditional eggnog contains alcohol (rum/bourbon), and Uncle Frank is on blood thinners after his knee replacement — alcohol interacts dangerously with anticoagulants. Honey-glazed ham is fine for everyone at the table. Cranberry walnut salad is fine for everyone. Mom's diabetes restriction has been lifted by her doctor, so the sugar in the cheesecake and honey glaze is not a concern for her.
required_elements: Beef Wellington with puff pastry is problematic for Tom: puff pastry contains wheat flour (gluten), and Tom has celiac disease
Smoked salmon crostini is problematic for Tom: crostini is bread-based and contains gluten (celiac)
Smoked salmon crostini should not be included on Rachel's saved plate: smoked salmon is a concern for pregnancy (Rachel is seven months pregnant)
Eggnog cheesecake is problematic for Uncle Frank: traditional eggnog contains alcohol, and Uncle Frank is on blood thinners after knee replacement surgery — alcohol interacts with blood thinners
Honey-glazed ham is fine for everyone currently attending the dinner
Cranberry walnut salad is fine for everyone
forbidden_elements: Flagging sugar content in eggnog cheesecake or honey-glazed ham as a problem for Mom (her diabetes restriction was removed by her doctor)
Saying Rachel cannot attend dinner as a reason to ignore her plate entirely (she requested a saved plate, so her pregnancy constraints still apply to that plate)
Flagging honey-glazed ham as problematic for anyone currently attending
Saying Uncle Frank should avoid cranberry walnut salad due to vitamin K in cranberries (cranberries are not high in vitamin K — leafy greens are the concern, not cranberries)
Treating smoked salmon as equivalent to raw fish for the table guests who have no fish restrictions
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across a family Christmas dinner planning conversation. The agent must track: (1) Tom has celiac disease → no gluten → no wheat/pastry/bread (inferential chain), (2) Rachel is seven months pregnant → no raw/smoked fish, no unpasteurized dairy (inferential), (3) Uncle Frank joins late on blood thinners → avoid alcohol and excessive vitamin K (inferential, late-joining entity), (4) Rachel EXITS the dinner but wants a saved plate → her pregnancy constraints still apply to her plate (scope change — EXIT with persistence), (5) Mom's diabetes restriction is REMOVED mid-conversation (doctor cleared her). At probe time, the current constraint state is: Tom = celiac (no gluten), Rachel = pregnant (saved plate only, no smoked fish on her plate), Uncle Frank = blood thinners (no alcohol), Mom = no restrictions. The five menu items produce mixed verdicts: beef Wellington (FAIL — gluten for Tom), smoked salmon crostini (FAIL — gluten for Tom AND smoked fish for Rachel's plate), eggnog cheesecake (FAIL — alcohol for Uncle Frank), honey-glazed ham (PASS), cranberry walnut salad (PASS). The key traps are: not flagging Mom's sugar (removed constraint), correctly scoping Rachel's restriction to her saved plate only, catching the alcohol in eggnog for Uncle Frank (late-joining entity), and not over-generalizing Uncle Frank's vitamin K concern to cranberries.

mechanism: Entity EXIT with scope change: person leaves but wants something packed/saved
